arrows.statement: evaluate the polynomial functor at C^d

Sigma_{N,d} is the weight monoid of the U-invariant subalgebra Sym(wedge^N C^d)^U, graded by degree; it is a monoid because Sym is a domain and the product of two highest-weight vectors is a nonzero highest-weight vector of the sum weight, and it is FINITELY GENERATED by Hadziev-Grosshans

arrows.note: this is the honest content of 'one stable object'. It is elementary, and it is why the stable object is NOT where the difficulty lives
arrows.statement: Sigma_{N,d} = Sigma_N^stab intersect {ell(lambda) <= d}. The multiplicity of V_lambda in Sym^k(wedge^N C^d) is the plethysm coefficient <s_lambda, h_k[e_N]>, which does not depend on d, and S_lambda(C^d) = 0 exactly when ell(lambda) > d. So the whole family is the length truncation of ONE d-independent monoid
a finitely generated monoid spans a rational polyhedral cone, and {ell <= d} is a face of the dominant cone, so cone(Sigma_{N,d}) = cone(Sigma_N^stab) intersect {lambda_{d+1} = 0}

arrows.consequence: finite generation of the SEMIGROUP is strictly stronger than finite generation of the CONE, and only the cone is needed for facets. Any compression theorem must say which one it is about
arrows.obstruction: the quantization period exceeds the spectrum denominator at these vertices, so (lambda_int, q) is a dominant lattice point of the cone with multiplicity zero
arrows.statement: the cone determines the semigroup, that is, Sigma_{N,d} is saturated
the normalized k = 1 slice of cone(Sigma_{N,d}) is the fermionic moment polytope

arrows.note: this is finiteness at each fixed d and carries no uniformity in d whatsoever
arrows.statement: the moment cone of a FIXED representation has a finite irredundant inequality list, computable

check.method: exact affine Farkas over the rationals

arrows.consequence: compression DOWN the rank ladder is a theorem: the published (3,10) system implies the (3,9), (3,8), (3,7) and (3,6) systems, and (4,10) implies (4,9) and (4,8)
arrows.direction: downward, rank d+1 to rank d
arrows.statement: Delta(N,d) = Delta(N,d+1) intersect {lambda_{d+1} = 0}, because an orbital of occupation zero is annihilated by its own annihilation operator; hence restricting the rank d+1 system to lambda_{d+1} = 0 cuts out exactly Delta(N,d)

arrows.direction: upward by zero padding, rank d to rank d+1
arrows.obstruction: a published row names orbitals by POSITION relative to d, so padding silently re-points it at a different orbital
arrows.statement: a valid row at rank d, padded with a zero coefficient, is valid at rank d+1

corrected_against.overstatement_retracted: 'no covariant map exists' is FALSE. The TIGHT extension is total and carries facets to facets 612 of 612. It is not a coefficient-level template rule: t* is defined by optimizing against Delta(N,d+1), so it organizes known rows rather than generating new ranks, and the NO-GO is unaffected
corrected_against.replication: its naive_padding_control independently reports the same 10 of 31 at (3,8) -> (3,9)
corrected_against.upgrade: its Theorem 1 proves only the TERMINAL insertion is a morphism, so the fixed-N ordered category is a poset and the non-trailing insertions tested here are not morphisms at all

broken_pairs: (3,6) -> (3,7): 1 of 1 rows have NO valid embedding
(3,8) -> (3,9): 15 of 31 rows have NO valid embedding
(3,9) -> (3,10): 5 of 52 rows have NO valid embedding
(4,8) -> (4,9): 7 of 15 rows have NO valid embedding
(4,9) -> (4,10): 25 of 60 rows have NO valid embedding

arrows.note: POST-HOC block, added after the pre-registered zero-padding prediction failed
arrows.obstruction: the inequality side of the census carries no covariant OI structure AT THE LEVEL OF COEFFICIENT PATTERNS; as a row functor it is contravariant
arrows.statement: for a valid row at rank d there is SOME order-preserving injection [d] -> [d+1] carrying it to a valid row

measured_symptoms.reading: the symmetric template stock is far smaller than the row count, which is encouraging, but it does not saturate inside the census window and the templates alone do not say WHICH instances are facets

arrows.obstruction: no known theorem supplies it; see the audit arrows below, all of which fail for the same reason
arrows.statement: there is a finite list of templates, and a decision rule of bounded complexity, that together produce the facet list of Delta(N,d) for every d

arrows.caution: the literature describes moment polytopes as having exponentially many facets, but that assertion was not verified for the fermionic family in this session
arrows.consequence: contrapositive: superpolynomial facet growth in d REFUTES finite templating. This converts the compression question into a facet-counting growth question, which is the smallest decisive experiment
arrows.statement: if every facet of the ambient Weyl-invariant moment cone at every rank is an instance under S_d of a fixed finite template list of maximum symmetric arity a, then that cone has O(d^a) facets, since an orbit of an arity-a template has at most binom(d,a) * a! members

arrows.finiteness_proved: descending chains of GL-stable Zariski-closed subsets stabilize; equations up to orbit
arrows.object_covered: wedge^N C^infinity as a polynomial functor: YES
arrows.obstruction: a facet of a moment cone is a real convex-geometric datum, not a Zariski-closed condition, and the family d -> Delta(N,d) is not a descending chain of closed subsets of anything. Finitely many equations up to symmetry says nothing about finitely many inequalities up to symmetry
arrows.statement: topological noetherianity of polynomial functors implies finite facet templates

arrows.finiteness_proved: ideals generated in bounded degree up to GL_infinity
arrows.object_covered: subvarieties of the infinite wedge closed under the Plucker operations: YES, and this is the closest existing result to the stable object
arrows.obstruction: same as X1. In addition the fermionic moment polytope is the moment image of the FULL projective space P(wedge^N C^d), not of a proper subvariety, so there is no interesting Plucker variety in play here at all; the equations these theorems bound are equations of objects the GPC problem does not use
arrows.statement: bounded Plucker varieties and the infinite wedge give finite facet templates

arrows.finiteness_proved: submodules of finitely generated modules are finitely generated
arrows.obstruction: two independent failures. First, module generation allows arbitrary R-linear combinations while a cone needs NONNEGATIVE ones, so finite module generation of the span of the facet normals does not bound the extreme rays of the dual cone. Second, and fatally, arrow A8oi shows the covariant OI action on the inequality side does not exist, so there is no OI-module to which the theorem could be applied
arrows.statement: FI or OI noetherianity gives finite facet templates

arrows.covers_A_N: A_2 yes, A_N for N >= 3 OPEN
arrows.object_covered: unbounded tcas; known only for Sym(Sym^2) and Sym(wedge^2)
arrows.obstruction: modules and ideals, not cones; the same gap as X3's first failure. Note the coincidence worth recording: the one fermionic case where tca noetherianity IS known, N = 2, is exactly the case where the GPC answer is classically trivial (lambda_{2i-1} = lambda_{2i}), and the project's main series N = 3 sits precisely in the open range
arrows.statement: noetherianity of the tca A_N gives finite facet templates

arrows.covers_the_weight_semigroup: the cone, yes; the semigroup, no
arrows.finiteness_proved: a finite irredundant inequality list at each fixed d
arrows.object_covered: the moment cone of one fixed representation
arrows.obstruction: the theorem quantifies over one representation. Arrows A8 and A8oi show the output is not even monotone in d for these tables, so no uniformity can be read off it
arrows.statement: the fixed-representation finite inequality list is uniform in d

arrows.kind: scope audit, and the practical alternative
arrows.obstruction: membership in a moment polytope is already in NP and coNP, with a polynomial-time weak membership oracle by scaling. So the physics question 'is this spectrum admissible at rank 40' does not need a facet list, and the compression program should say explicitly which of the two goals it is pursuing
arrows.statement: rank-20 or rank-40 usability requires the facet list

bulois-denis-ressayre.what: an algorithm computing the MINIMAL inequality list of the moment cone of any representation of a complex reductive group, with the fermionic cone GL_d acting on wedge^r C^d implemented explicitly
bulois-denis-ressayre.where: Bulois, Denis and Ressayre, An Algorithm to compute the Kronecker cone and other moment cones, 2025; arXiv:2505.08812

burgisser-et-al.checked: abstract; the exponential facet count is asserted for moment polytopes broadly and was NOT verified for the fermionic family specifically
burgisser-et-al.what: membership in a moment polytope is in NP and coNP, and there is a polynomial-time weak membership oracle by scaling, for a family described as having exponentially many facets

draisma-eggermont.what: bounded Plucker varieties are defined in bounded degree; the limit in the dual infinite wedge is cut out, up to symmetry, by finitely many equations
draisma-eggermont.where: Draisma and Eggermont, J. reine angew. Math. 737 (2018) 189-215

draisma-polynomial-functors.what: every finite-degree polynomial functor over an infinite field is topologically noetherian, so a GL-stable closed subset is cut out by finitely many orbits of equations

fi-oi-noetherianity.what: finitely generated FI-modules and OI-modules over noetherian rings are noetherian, and finitely generated symmetric ideals in infinite polynomial rings are finitely generated up to symmetry
fi-oi-noetherianity.where: Church-Ellenberg-Farb; Aschenbrenner-Hillar; Hillar-Sullivant, Adv. Math. 229 (2012); Draisma, Noetherianity up to symmetry, LNM 2108 (2014)

hadziev-grosshans.what: C[X]^U is finitely generated for an affine G-variety X, G reductive, U a maximal unipotent subgroup
hadziev-grosshans.where: Hadziev 1967; Grosshans, Algebraic Homogeneous Spaces and Invariant Theory, LNM 1673

horn-klyachko-ktw.checked: standard, from memory of the statement; the arity claim is read off the shape of the inequalities, not off a growth theorem
horn-klyachko-ktw.what: the Horn cone for sums of Hermitian matrices is cut out by the Horn inequalities indexed by triples (I,J,K) of subsets of size r for every r < n, and the essential ones are exactly those with Littlewood-Richardson coefficient 1. Their arity grows with r, hence is UNBOUNDED in n
horn-klyachko-ktw.where: Klyachko, Selecta Math. 4 (1998); Knutson-Tao, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 12 (1999); Knutson-Tao-Woodward, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 17 (2004)
horn-klyachko-ktw.why_here: the closest moment cone whose facets are COMPLETELY known, and it fails bounded-arity templating. Absent a reason why the fermionic cone should be better behaved, T1 should be expected false

mumford-ness-brion.checked: abstract, plus the exact finite check in this campaign
mumford-ness-brion.what: the moment polytope of a projective G-variety is the closure of the normalized highest weights occurring in its homogeneous coordinate ring
mumford-ness-brion.where: Mumford/Ness; Brion, Sur l'image de l'application moment; used in this project as Klyachko's practical algorithm

nagpal-sam-snowden.what: among unbounded twisted commutative algebras, noetherianity is known ONLY for Sym(Sym^2 C^infinity) and Sym(wedge^2 C^infinity); the degree three and higher cases, which include A_3 = Sym(wedge^3 C^infinity), are open
nagpal-sam-snowden.where: Nagpal, Sam and Snowden, Selecta Math. 22 (2016); and the skew-commutative sequel, Selecta Math. (2019)

nekrasov.what: the dual infinite wedge is GL_infinity-equivariantly noetherian, extending the bounded Plucker case

repo-census-sandwich.what: P = O at all nine census systems, so validity on the certified vertex set is validity on the polytope

repo-ordered-stability.checked: in-repo artifact, landed on main during this campaign
repo-ordered-stability.what: the fixed-N ordered category of mode embeddings degenerates to a POSET (only the terminal insertion carries Delta(N,d) into Delta(N,e)), so representation stability is vacuous there; chamber-facing rows are not permutation stable; and the TIGHT padding and frozen-core extensions are exact sections of the restrictions, carrying facets to facets 612 of 612

repo-quantization.what: the quantization period of a census vertex is the order of a finite isotropy character of its certified attainer; p = q at ten of fourteen measured vertices and 2q at the other four

repo-screening-orbit.what: screening is NOT a Weyl-orbit invariant: the dominant chamber is a fundamental domain and so is exactly what the Weyl group does not preserve, and the moment cone's Weyl invariance is a statement about the AMBIENT cone, not a chamber-facing list

reuvers.what: the GPC polytope volume approaches the Pauli hypersimplex volume as the one-body dimension grows, so the generalized constraints are volumetrically negligible except in few-fermion settings

vergne-walter.what: the moment cone of an arbitrary finite-dimensional unitary representation of a compact connected Lie group is cut out by finitely many linear inequalities, via a variant of Ressayre's dominant pairs
vergne-walter.where: Vergne and Walter, J. Symplectic Geom. 15 (2017); arXiv:1410.8144
